docs_outline: Orientation call. Returns a document's compact indented outline (alias/type/label per line, § marks section headings). IDs are stable; prefer them in follow-ups. Address the document by `id` or `path` (at least one; a `path` in either form). For the whole document body in one call, use docs_read.
docs_read: Read a whole document in one call: `raw` is the complete file bytes verbatim (fences/tables/list markers preserved), `properties` is the document's property bag grouped by source — `{ frontmatter, inline, computed }` — plus `id`/`path`/`rev` (the document's row attributes, spelled as the query language spells them). What `properties.frontmatter` holds is format-dependent: for markdown it's the parsed frontmatter fence; for YAML/JSON it's the parsed object the file represents; other adapters extract per their format. `inline` holds dataview-style `key:: value` fields from the body; `computed` holds engine intrinsics (`title`, `tags`). The cold-start 'read the guide before doing anything' call. Address the document by `id` or `path` (at least one; a query hit's `id`/`path` are the values to pass). Pass include_ids:true to also get the document's block ids in order (`ids`) AND `hashes` — a {block `id` → block `hash`} map giving the exact `expect.content_hash` value the raw `apply` kernel needs, so one read yields both the ids and the CAS tokens to mutate them (no follow-up blocks_read_many hydration) — AND `parents`, a {block id → parent block id | null} map (null = top level), because `ids` is a flat pre-order walk and a list is otherwise indistinguishable from its items; filter to `parents[id] === null` for the top-level blocks. For structure-only orientation use docs_outline; to hydrate a single block use blocks_read.
docs_read_many: Batch whole-document read — the hydrate half of query→hydrate. The plural of docs_read: pass `docs`, a list of refs (each a document id OR a path, in either form), and get back one full read per ref. Returns `{ items, errors, truncated }`: each found doc is a full docs_read projection (`raw` = complete file bytes verbatim, `properties` grouped by source, plus `id`/`path`/`rev`, and — with include_ids:true — the document's ordered block `ids`, a `hashes` {block `id` → block `hash`} map for raw-`apply` CAS pinning, and a `parents` {block id → parent block id | null} map so top-level vs nested blocks are distinguishable without an outline read); a ref that resolves to no live document lands in `errors` as {ref, error:"doc_not_found"} WITHOUT failing the call, so one bad ref never sinks the batch. Duplicate refs collapse first-seen (a repeated ref yields a single item). Capped at 100 refs per call; excess refs are dropped and `truncated` is set. Pass budget_tokens to cap total hydrated size — the batch stops early and flags `truncated` when the next doc would exceed it; the FIRST doc always ships even when it alone exceeds the budget (the same at-least-one-row contract as docs_list/docs_tree, so a budgeted caller always makes progress). Use this after query/blocks_search/blocks_resolve to pull N whole docs in ONE round-trip instead of N serial docs_read calls; for a single doc use docs_read, and for lean structure-only orientation use docs_outline (docs_get_many before surface 3.0).
blocks_read: Hydrate one block subtree at a resolution (skeleton|outline|text|raw|full). `id` is the block's id (`b_…`) and its document is inferred from it; an `n_` node id is not a block id — nodes_block_read reads the block a node was projected from (nodes_get before surface 3.0: blocks used to be called nodes here, and `nodes` now names the extracted-entity rows). Every resolution carries the block's `id` and `type`; raw and full add `raw` (its source bytes) and `hash` (its own raw hash) — the value update/split need in expect.content_hash, so you can fetch it before editing rather than reading it back from a conflict; full adds `text`, `attrs`, `ordinal`, `depth` and `parent_id` (null at the top level). Use this to expand the lean ids returned by query/blocks_resolve. To read a whole document in one call, use docs_read (blocks_read on a heading's id returns only that block, not its section).
nodes_block_read: Read the block a NODE was projected from: `id` is the node's id (`n_…`, from `query` over `from nodes`) and the result is exactly what blocks_read returns for that block — the same resolutions (skeleton|outline|text|raw|full, default full), the same `id`/`type`/`raw`/`hash`/`text`/`attrs`/`ordinal`/`depth`/`parent_id`. The hop from an occurrence (an `md:link`, `md:task`, `md:section`, … node) to the editable block that holds it, in one call; blocks_read itself takes a block id only. An unknown node, or a node that names no live block (a block-less node, such as one derived from the frontmatter), is block_missing.
blocks_read_many: Fetch up to 100 blocks by id (in request order) with budget truncation — the plural of blocks_read (nodes_get_many before surface 3.0). Block ids are globally unique, so `ids` may span ANY number of documents — each id is resolved to its owning doc server-side. Result carries `nodes` (the hydrated blocks, one per resolved id), `truncated` (cap or `budget_tokens` hit — the first resolved block always ships even when it alone exceeds the budget, so a budgeted caller always makes progress), and `unresolved` — the requested ids that name no live block (never silently dropped).
docs_tree: ORIENTATION: the path-separator-aware shape of a repo in ONE small call — start here to answer 'what does this repo contain?', NOT with docs_list. Like `tree -L <depth>` crossed with `du`: every live document under `path` (a directory prefix; omit for the repo root) is collapsed at `depth` path segments (default 1 = immediate children), giving one entry per directory and one per shallow document. Returns `{ prefix, depth, total: { docs, blocks }, entries: [{ id?, path, kind: "dir"|"doc", docs, blocks, updated_at }], truncated, cursor }`: a `dir` entry's `path` ends in `/` (no `id`) and its `docs`/`blocks`/`updated_at` are the totals + latest last-commit timestamp UNDER it; a `doc` entry is a single document (docs = 1) with its `id`. `total` always covers everything under `prefix` regardless of paging, so you see the true size of what you're looking at. On an 800-document repo `depth:1` at the root is ~10 rows where docs_list would be ~800; descend by calling again with `path` set to a dir entry (or raise `depth`). Entries are ordered by path and paged: `limit` (default 200) / `cursor` / `budget_tokens` with an honest `truncated`. For ranked or attribute-based discovery use `blocks_resolve`/`query`; to enumerate the documents themselves once you know where to look, use docs_list with a `path_glob`.
docs_list: ENUMERATE live documents (the `omg ls` operation) as a page: `{ items: [{ id, path, updated_at, blocks }], truncated, cursor }` — the document's id, its path (`/`-rooted, as every path the surface returns), last-commit timestamp (ISO, or null) and live block count — ordered by path. This is a flat `ls`, not an orientation primitive: unscoped on a large repo it is hundreds of rows, and the engine has no directory concept here — `path_glob` is a simple LIKE match where `*` matches ANY run INCLUDING `/` (so `projects/*` is the whole subtree; there is no 'immediate children only'). To learn a repo's shape, call docs_tree first, then scope this with a `path_glob` once you know where to look. Paged under the uniform list contract: `limit` (default 200) caps rows, `cursor` (from a truncated page) resumes after the last row returned, `budget_tokens` caps the page's estimated size (at least one row is always returned), and `truncated` is honest — when true you have NOT seen everything. For structured/ranked discovery use `query` or `blocks_resolve`.
query_syntax: Reference: the full `query` (OQX) syntax — the clause order, the sugar (a block without a consumer is collect, where-first bodies, brackets, postfix `!`, `is`/`is not`, `and`/`or`/`not`), `/`-rooted paths, targets and field namespaces, scalar semantics and absence, domain predicates incl. `refs()`, nested queries and the root row (`^docs`, `^id`, `0^docs`), `select`/`order by`/paging, `follow`, and worked examples. Call this before writing a non-trivial query. No arguments.
query: OQX (omgbase Query eXpressions) — composable query in ONE expression. Clause order is fixed: select, from, where, frontier, follow, order by, limit, offset — `select` first (`select path, era from docs where era > 1600 order by era desc limit 3`), its keyword optional only there; `from docs where … select …` is a parse error naming the order. Two rules: DOT navigation belongs to the host object model (`doc.layer`, `section.blocks`, `dst.title`); WHITESPACE query directives belong to OQX — a nested query is `<receiver> collect|exists|count|first|single { <block> }` (a postfix directive + a `{ … }` block), never a method. The clauses, in writing order: `select` projects the hit's columns (`select path, title`; an alias per computed item, `n: size(tags)`; no `select` = the bare envelope); `from E` selects a property/relation relative to the current source scope and flattens it (a typed flatMap): top-level `from docs|blocks|nodes|links` selects the repository's docs/blocks/nodes/links (the `links` target is the authored link graph as first-class rows — one row per link RELATION; the `md:link` node is a link's occurrence in the text, `via_id` points at it, and a frontmatter link has a row and no node — `id`/`path` plus the plain fields doc_id/block_id/via_id/dst_id/dst_path/uri/predicate/provenance/dst_kind/anchor/field, with path/doc.* reaching the SOURCE doc and `dst` the destination DOCUMENT row when the link points at one — `dst.title`, `dst.layer`, `dst_kind == "document"`; absent for an external or block destination and for a dangling target); `where` filters the rows; then `frontier`, `follow`, `order by`, `limit`/`offset` (each below). Its distinctive power is receiver-constrained nested queries that correlate to the current row: `from docs where nodes exists { where kind == "md:task" }` returns only the docs that themselves contain a matching node (not a global scan). Directives: `exists { … }` / `count { … }` in where — with an optional count comparison `nodes count { where kind == "md:task" } >= 2`; `collect { … }` in select for hierarchical results, nestable (`select secs: nodes collect { select h: name, items: section.blocks collect { where type == "list_item" } where kind == "md:section" } from docs`). CLAUSE ORDER IS FIXED (ADR-020): within one body — the top level or any `{ block }` — clauses appear at most once each, in exactly this order: `select … from … where … frontier … follow … order by … limit N offset N` (`frontier <pred>` is a clause of a body that has a `follow` — it marks the body's SEEDS, oqx 0.20). Every clause is optional except a top-level `from`; an out-of-order clause is a parse error naming the order. ONLY `select` may drop its keyword, and only when it is the first clause written (`path, open from docs where …`; `nodes collect { attrs.text }` projects `attrs.text`). Every other clause carries its keyword, with one piece of sugar (oqx 0.17): a block's leading expression is its `where` when it is predicate-shaped (`nodes exists { kind == "md:task" }` ≡ `nodes exists { where kind == "md:task" }`); a bare name or dotted path is a projection, so filter on a bare field with `is active`, and `{ name where … }` is the projection + filter (`{ age >= 18, name }` is an error). A top-level predicate needs `where` (`where` follows `from`, so `age > 15 from people` is an error), a bare boolean property in leading position PROJECTS (`nodes collect { active }`), and `from docs count` is an error (write `docs count { … }` for the consumer, or `select count from docs` to project a field named count). More sugar, each desugaring in the parser to the explicit directive: a receiver block without a consumer is `collect` (`docs { type == "x" }`, `nodes { kind == "md:task" }`, `size(nodes { is checked })` — wherever a value stands, and after a `follow` destination too: `follow children { depth 2 }` is that destination's block; `x distinct { … }` is `x collect distinct { … }`); a tuple `(a, b)` (two or more expressions, concatenated one level flat) is a value and a receiver (`"x" in (tags, aliases)`, `follow (before, after) { depth 2 }`); brackets `x[p]` = `x first { where p }` (the first match or absent), `x[p]!` = `x single { where p }` required (exactly one, else filter_invalid), `x[n]` = `x first { offset n }` (positional; out of range is absent); postfix `x!` = required (the value, or a loud error naming the expression and the row — never a filter, never a coercion; tightest: `a!.b` vs `a.b!`); prefix `is x` / `not x` (truthiness); infix `x is y` / `x is not y` compares identity (`$key`: a store row's id, else the value — `x is null` is the absence test; for scalars `is` ≡ `==`); and a `select` item may use the items to its left (`boss: ^docs[slug == ^manager], name: boss.title`). `and` / `or` / `not` are the connectives; `&&` / `||` / `!` are accepted synonyms (the canonical printer writes the words). `where` may reference the same body's `select` aliases (`select path, old: era < 1000 from docs where old` — inlined at parse time; an alias shadows a same-named field there). On the nodes/blocks targets a bare identifier that is not a structural field (doc_id, block_id, kind/name/value; doc_id, type/text, ordinal/depth) or row attribute (id, path, raw, hash, updated_at) reads the flattened attrs bag — `checked` == `attrs.checked`, `level` == `attrs.level` — so the name you filter on matches the name a projection returns (`select attrs.checked` yields key `checked`); the `attrs.<key>` form still works and an absent key is silently false. Any consumer accepts `distinct` to dedup the rows it reduces by their projected value — `nodes count distinct { select kind }`, `nodes collect distinct { select kind }`, top-level `select distinct type` (empty projection dedups by identity). `values` after a projection of exactly ONE item returns the bare value instead of a `{name: value}` record: at the top level `select path values from docs where layer == "canon"` returns `values: ["a.md", …]` (paged like hits; `hits` is empty), and inside a block `select tags: tags collect { $it values }` yields a plain array. `$it` is the current item itself — the row, or the scalar element when the receiver is a list property (`where tags exists { where $it == "pricing" }`); inside a block `^$it` is the enclosing row. `none { … }` is the zero-cardinality test — true iff the block yields no rows (≡ `!… exists { … }`), and how "every" is spelled: `nodes none { where kind == "md:task" and not checked }` = no open tasks; also a whole-query directive (`docs none { … }` returns `none`). `limit N` / `offset N` bound a row set AFTER where/order/distinct and BEFORE the consumer reduces it, so they mean the same under every consumer: at the top level (`order by era desc limit 3` — the tool's `limit`/`cursor` then page within that bounded set) or inside any block (`nodes collect { … order by ordinal limit 1 }`; `nodes exists { offset 1 }` = at least two). `entries(x)` turns a record into a collection of entries — inside the block `$key` is the property key and `$it` (and bare names) the value: `select fm: entries(frontmatter) collect { k: $key, v: $it }`, `from nodes where kind == "md:task" and entries(attrs) exists { where $key == "checked" and $it }`; works on `data` (the merged authored bag: frontmatter + inline) / `frontmatter` / `inline` (nested dotted keys folded back — an authored `$`-prefixed key such as `$version` is reached as `frontmatter.$version` and listed by `entries(frontmatter)`; a bare `$version` is an unknown OQX name and reads nothing), `attrs`, a nested frontmatter map, or a list (numeric index keys). Plain objects never auto-iterate; `entries()` is the explicit bridge. The where clause is a boolean tree: compose scalar predicates and consumer directives with `and`, `or`, `not`, and grouping (`layer == "canon" or nodes exists { where kind == "md:task" }`). Relative source: `from E` inside a top-level consumer block re-projects the rows — `docs collect { from nodes where kind == "md:task" }` starts at docs, projects each doc through its `nodes` relation, and queries the resulting nodes (a scalar relation like `from doc` contributes one row; a missing/non-navigable relation is a loud error, never a global scan). One-scope lift: a `collect` in `where` with a `^name` both filters (non-empty) and binds the matching values into the parent select in one expression — `select path, open from docs where nodes collect { ^open: value where kind == "md:task" and not attrs.checked }` returns the docs with an open task, each carrying its open-task texts. Correlation / joins (the `^` sigil, symmetric with the lift): a nested query may READ a name bound one scope outward — bind it in the parent (a select value or a lift), then reference `^name` inside a nested query's where. Combined with the root row's collections `^docs` / `^nodes` / `^blocks` / `^links` (the repository is OQX's root row, one scope out from a top-level row — one caret per enclosing block, or the absolute `0^docs` from any depth; an UNBOUNDED repository scan, uncorrelated until you add a `^` predicate) this expresses lateral/dependent joins without a JOIN keyword: `^<t> exists { where … == ^k }` = semi-join, `not … exists { … }` = anti-join, `… collect { … }` in select = nested left-join, and the select-only lookups `first { … }` / `single { … }` (zero-or-one / one-to-one; `single` errors if it matches >1) — e.g. `select owner_id, owner: ^nodes single { where kind == "person" and attrs.id == ^owner_id } from docs`. Membership over a lifted set: `<value> in ^keys`. `^` reads exactly ONE scope out (no arbitrary-ancestor search), and a bare name reads the CURRENT row only — it never falls through to an enclosing row or the root, so reach outward explicitly with `^name` (the enclosing row) or `^docs` / `0^docs` (the root row's collections; `^id` / `0^id` is the repository id, `^$it` the root object). A bare `docs` INSIDE a block is an error ("did you mean `^docs`"), never an empty read; `$repo` (surface < 2.0) is refused with the replacement spelled out. PATHS are `/`-rooted on the surface (surface 2.0): every path returned — `path`, an edge's `dst_path`, a hit's `path` — is the reference form (`/a/b.md`), and a string literal compared with `path`/`dst_path` by `==`/`!=` or passed to their `startsWith` accepts both forms (`path == "a.md"` and `path == "/a.md"` both match); a property's value is the author's, so a reference held in frontmatter compares with `^path` directly (`^docs { ^path in list(after) }` = the documents whose `after` names me). `refs(field)` resolves the document REFERENCES a property holds (a string or a list of `/a.md`, `a.md` or `d_…` elements; dangling and non-string elements dropped) to live docs rows, so it is a source (`from refs("/a.md")`), a receiver (`refs(before) collect { path, when }`, `refs(see_also)[0]`) or a `follow` destination (`follow refs(before), refs(after)` walks a timeline both ways); `follow before` over the strings fails — a hit must be a document, block, node or edge row. Top-level consumers: the whole query can be a consumer directive over a bare root receiver (a target name at the root scope) to change its result shape — `docs count { … }`, `docs exists { … }` and `docs none { … }` reduce to a scalar (returned as `count`/`exists`/`none`, no hits), `docs first { … }` / `docs single { … }` return zero-or-one hit (`single` errors if the query matches >1); a bare `from …` is the collect form. (A bare target at the root scope is the same collection `^<target>` reaches from inside where/select.) Scalar predicates follow the @omgbase/oqx semantics (strict typed equality with absence normalized so `!=` over an absent field matches; case-sensitive string ops with `.lower()`/`.upper()` and a regex `matches()`; absent sorts last; arithmetic supported), including doc.<key> reach-through and `text("terms")` — a full-text (FTS5) PRUNING predicate that, because it is an ordinary predicate, composes inside correlated subqueries and collects (e.g. `nodes exists { where kind == "md:task" and text("ship") }`), which the flat `query` tool cannot express. (`text` prunes; relevance ranking is separate.) And `semantic("phrase")` — an embedding cosine SCORE (docs/blocks only) usable as a threshold prune (`semantic("the great work") > 0.6`) or a projection (`select score: semantic("…")`); it needs an embedding provider that has embedded this repository (else `provider_unavailable`, naming what to configure — never a silent unranked result) and, like `text`, composes inside nested scopes. Ranking: `order by <expr> [asc|desc], …` sorts the result (`order by semantic("the great work") desc` = semantic top-K; also orders by any frontmatter field / `path`), always tie-broken by (path, id) for a total order — this is how score functions become a ranking. A custom order disables the keyset cursor (you still get the top `limit` with `truncated`). Recursion (`follow`): make the query recursive over a TYPE-PRESERVING relation (the relation's successor type must equal the query target). `from blocks where id == "b_x" follow block.children` walks the block subtree from a seed; the `where` picks the SEED rows and `follow <relation>` expands them. A bare `follow <relation>` carries no sub-clauses; a brace after any destination opens that destination's block (oqx 0.20 — there is no options block), an ordinary block with two clauses of its own after `where`: `follow <rel> { where <pred> }` filters which successors keep participating at each hop (running out ⇒ a leaf), `{ frontier <pred> }` cuts a relation that could otherwise continue (⇒ a frontier; only occurrences this destination reached), `{ depth <n> }` bounds the walk through this destination (1..8, default 8). `follow distinct` dedups reached rows by identity (the default keeps one occurrence per distinct walk path). Identity is `$key` — a store row's id; a block may project `$key: <expr>` to rekey the rows it yields (a destination block's `$key:` is not a column) — e.g. `follow out_links collect { $key: group from dst }` treats same-`group` documents as one node. Each reached row carries recursion metadata: `$depth` (seed = 1), the categorical `$stop` (interior | leaf | frontier | depth | cycle) with `$leaf`/`$frontier` boolean sugar, and `$ordinal` (a deterministic 1..N rank over the walk, ordered by depth then path — `order by $ordinal` for walk order, `where $ordinal <= N` for a deterministic budget cut). It is queryable in select / order by AND filterable post-walk in the top-level `where` (a `where` conjunct referencing a recursion intrinsic filters the walk's RESULT — `from blocks where type == "list_item" and $leaf follow block.children` = the leaves; the non-recursion conjuncts remain the seed predicate). Recursion intrinsics are NOT valid in a destination block's `where` or `frontier` (those run mid-walk, before the metadata exists), nor inside a consumer directive. Cyclic graphs are safe: a revisited node is admitted once as a `$stop == "cycle"` occurrence and never re-expanded. Type-preserving relations today: `block.children` (blocks→blocks, immediate child blocks), `section.children` (nodes→nodes, immediate child sections — a true outline depth ladder) and `section.subsections` (nodes→nodes, the whole transitive sub-tree — flattens to depth 2). The authored citation graph is walked through the LINK ROWS with a destination block (docs→docs): `follow out_links collect { from dst }` reaches the documents a doc links TO (`dst` is a link's destination document; an external or dangling link has none and contributes no successor), `follow in_links collect { from doc }` its backlinks (`doc` is the link's source); `depth`/`frontier` are clauses of the block — `follow out_links collect { from dst depth 2 }`; filter the rows first for a predicate-restricted walk (`follow out_links collect { from dst where predicate == "depends_on" }`). There is no `out`/`in` relation (surface 3.0 — a doc's `out`/`in` is an ordinary absent property). Consumers compose over the walk (`blocks count { where … follow block.children }`). A `follow` may also nest inside a select-position `collect` for a per-row recursive subtree: `select outline: nodes collect { select n: name, d: $depth where kind == "md:section" and name == "Overview" follow section.children } from docs` (the collect's `where` seeds, correlated to the row; `follow` recurses; the collect's `select` projects each occurrence). Receivers: from docs — `nodes`, `blocks`, `doc.out_links`/`doc.in_links` (a doc's outgoing/incoming links as rows; the documents at their other end are `out_links collect distinct { from dst }` / `in_links collect distinct { from doc }`); from links — `doc` (the source document) and `dst` (the destination document, when there is one); from nodes — `section.blocks` (content under an `md:section` node's heading, transitively including deeper headings), `section.children` (immediate child sections), and `section.subsections` (all contained sections); from blocks — `section` (enclosing `md:section` node(s)), `block.children` (child blocks), `block.nodes` (the projected nodes anchored to this block — links/tasks/anchors/…), and `block.out_links` (this block's outgoing links as rows — body links + inline fields; frontmatter links are doc-grain, use `doc.out_links`); from any row — `^docs` / `^nodes` / `^blocks` / `^links` (the root row's collections; `0^docs` from any depth). Returns lean hits {id, path, ...projections} — the envelope keys are the attributes, so a hit's `id` pastes into the next `where id == …` unchanged, and is the value a tool's `id` argument takes (the name rule, surface 3.0: omgbase adds no `$` names — `$` belongs to OQX's `$it`/`$key`/`$depth`…; every engine attribute is bare snake_case and WINS on collision — id/path everywhere, raw/hash/updated_at on docs and blocks, title/tags/format on docs — and an authored key of the same name is reached through `data.<k>` / `frontmatter.<k>` / `inline.<k>`; `select id, path` is simply the envelope and any other projection whose key would be id/path must be aliased (`p: data.path`); every tool result spells a row with the same names) — with truncated + cursor (or a `count`/`exists` scalar for those consumers). Covers structural + section navigation + ad-hoc correlation + bounded recursive traversal (`follow`).
graph: Neighborhood macro: the bounded graph AROUND one or more root documents in ONE call — { documents, links, frontier } — so you can orient without hand-writing an OQX `follow`. This is a CONVENIENCE WRAPPER, not a new engine: it compiles its args into an OQX `follow out_links collect { from dst }` / `follow in_links collect { from doc }` query and runs it through the same `query` path (the returned `queries` field is the exact follow query it generated). It does NOT replace `follow` or `from links` — reach for the `query` tool directly when you need successor/frontier predicates, `$key`-keyed identity, `$ordinal` budgets, cross-document correlation, or the links scan with its own projections. `roots` are one or more doc refs (paths and/or ids); they are depth 0. `degrees` is the max hop distance (root = 0; maps to `follow … collect { … depth degrees+1 }`, capped so degrees+1 ≤ 8; default 1). `direction` is `out` (outgoing links), `in` (backlinks), or `both` (default). `predicate` restricts the neighborhood to documents reachable from a root via edges of that predicate (both the documents and the edges are filtered). `select` adds document projections (OQX select expressions, e.g. "layer", "path"). `max_documents` caps the distinct document set (default 200) with a `truncated` flag. Returns: `documents` (each with `id`/`path`/`degree` = min hops from a root/`frontier` bool + your projections — a bare-name selection such as "title" is its own key, `id`/`path` land on the envelope keys, and any other expression is `sel_<i>`), `links` (the traversed links as rows of the `links` target under its own field names — `id`, `doc_id`/`block_id` (the source), `via_id`, `dst_id`, `dst_path`, `uri`, `dst_kind`, `predicate`, `provenance`, `anchor`, `field`; external `x_…` and dangling phantom endpoints are preserved as edge stubs, exactly as `from links` surfaces them), and `frontier` (the documents on the outer boundary — `{ id, path, degree }`, min degree == degrees; at degrees 0 that is the roots themselves).
blocks_search: Full-text (FTS5, bm25-ranked) keyword search over block text: `{ hits: [{ id (the block), doc_id, path, type, text, score }], truncated }`. Input is treated as a search box — plain words are ANDed, "quoted phrases" match adjacency, punctuation like / is safe (no query DSL). For structured filtering or frontmatter projection use `query` instead (see query_syntax). (text_search before surface 3.0.)
blocks_resolve: Resolve a name/title/concept to the concrete blocks it refers to — 'the id of the thing I mean'. Hybrid ranker (FTS + semantic when a provider is configured); best on short, entity-shaped inputs (a title, term, or phrase). Returns ranked `{ id, locator, preview, evidence }` (the block's id, its `path#type[ordinal]` locator); prefer the returned ids in follow-up calls. For open natural-language questions or passage retrieval, use `query` with `semantic` instead. (resolve before surface 3.0.)
apply: The only real writer. Takes exactly one of two inputs. `effects` (preferred): an ORDERED list of intentional writes — `create insert set unset move remove split merge retarget` over documents, blocks, nodes and sections (the vocabulary `plan` documents) — planned and committed as ONE transaction with one commit: dry_run:true returns the frozen Plan (what `plan` returns; nothing written), without it the result is the Receipt `{ plan_id, commit, revisions: [{ id, path, hash }], new_ids: { "$new.n": id }, committed: true }`. `ops` (the kernel, legacy input): a changeset of kernel ops (insert/update/move/remove/split/merge) applied atomically — all apply or none. Each op is a tagged object keyed by "op"; the block an op targets is named by its `block` (update/split) or `blocks` (move/remove/merge) field, never `id`/`target` (the op grammar is spec/mutate's, unchanged by the surface's `id`/`path` argument rule). Ops apply in order; later ops see earlier effects; minted ids are referenceable via "$n.ids[i]". Pass dry_run:true first for multi-doc changes to preview diffs. The `ops` result is `{ results: [{ ids, … }], revisions: [{ id, path, hash }], diffs?, committed }` — one revision per touched document with its hash after the change (the same shape a changes_since revision has). update/split/merge/remove take a CAS `expect.content_hash` — get it from docs_read include_ids (its `hashes` map) in the same read that gave you the ids, or use the ref-accepting block_* sugar (blocks_update/blocks_split/…) which pins it server-side (effects pin it for you). Conflicts carry current truth (`data.current.hash` + `markdown`) — including a missing/omitted expect.content_hash, whose error returns the current hash — so retry from the error, don't re-read.
plan: Plan a write without writing: lower an ORDERED list of `effects` — the intentional-write vocabulary `create insert set unset move remove split merge retarget` over documents, blocks, nodes and sections (spec/mutate §11) — to the kernel ops and document operations they mean, check their preconditions now (a stale `expect` fails here as it would at commit), reject contradictory effects (`conflicting_effects`: two writes to one scalar with different values, an effect addressing a target an earlier one removed — an identical duplicate is dropped with a diagnostic), and return the frozen Plan: `{ version: 1, planner_v, effects (targets resolved; `$new.n` kept symbolic), opset, preconditions: { docs, blocks, parents, absent_paths }, new_ids: [{ symbol, kind }], plan_id, diagnostics, preview: { results, revisions, diffs } }`. `plan_id` is the sha256 of the plan's executable core, so an identical plan over identical state has the same id and a plan burns no real id (new identities are `$new.0, $new.1, …`, minted at execute and mapped in the receipt). Hand the whole Plan to `execute` (or just its `plan_id` with the same `effects`); nothing has expiry — the preconditions decide. Effect shapes: { op: "create", path, markdown, frontmatter? }, { op: "insert", into: Target, at? = "end", markdown, expect? }, { op: "set", target, field, value, expect? } (fields: a document's `frontmatter.<key>` or `content`, a block's `markdown` or `attrs.checked`, a node's editable property), { op: "unset", target: document, field: "frontmatter.<key>" }, { op: "move", target: document, to, retarget_inbound? = true }, { op: "move", targets: [block…], into, at?, expect? }, { op: "remove", target: document } | { targets: [block…], expect? }, { op: "split", target: block, at: [byte…] }, { op: "merge", targets: [block…], separator? }, { op: "retarget", repairs: [{ from, to }], path_glob? }; Target = { kind: "document", id? | path? } | { kind: "block", id } | { kind: "node", id } | { kind: "section", heading_id }; `expect` carries `content_hash`, `parent_children_hash` and/or the document's `revision`. Block content hashes you omit are pinned from the live rows. The plan's core keeps paths in the storage form (they are digested); only `preview` is rooted.
execute: Commit exactly a plan made by `plan` (or by `apply { effects, dry_run: true }`), as one transaction with one commit. Two forms, exactly one of them: `plan` — the Plan object as returned (`preview` may be dropped; `version` other than 1 → `unsupported_plan_version`, an edited core whose digest no longer equals its `plan_id` → `plan_mismatch`); or `plan_id` + `effects` — the engine re-plans the effects and commits only when the new plan's digest equals `plan_id` (else `plan_mismatch { expected, actual }`: the effects or the documents they target changed). Every precondition the plan froze is re-validated inside the transaction; a document that moved on fails `stale_plan` (retriable: re-plan) with nothing written, and replaying an already executed plan fails the same way. Returns the Receipt `{ plan_id, commit, revisions: [{ id, path, hash }], new_ids: { "$new.0": "b_…", … }, committed: true }` — `new_ids` maps the plan's symbolic identities to the ids minted. The commit records the plan as its intent (`commits.ops`).
blocks_insert: Insert new block(s) parsed from `markdown` under a parent, at a position. `to` names the parent: a BLOCK ref (id or locator) nests the new blocks under that block — it must be a CONTAINER (a list, list item, task, blockquote or table); a leaf such as a heading or paragraph fails `type_mismatch` (spec/mutate §1.1) — use blocks_append for "into this heading's section / this container" or `at: {after: <ref>}` for "right after this block"; or a DOCUMENT ref (doc id or path) places them at the document's top level — so appending a new section to a document is `{ to: "<path>", markdown: "## New\n\n…" }` (the positional generalization of docs_append). `at` places among the parent's children: "end" (default) / "start" / {before|after: <block ref>}. Optional `expect.parent_children_hash` is the destination-parent CAS: the parent's CURRENT direct child ids (the document's top-level ids for a document `to`) joined by "," and sha256-hexed — compute it from docs_read include_ids (`ids` filtered by `parents`) — and the insert fails `stale_expectation` (with `data.current.parent_children_hash`) if the siblings changed under you; `content_hash` has no meaning here (there is no target block) and is not accepted. Expands to one insert op through the kernel writer.
blocks_update: Replace a block's markdown (and/or set attrs) with compare-and-swap. `id` is the block's id (or any ref resolve accepts); `expect.content_hash` is pinned to the block's current bytes server-side when omitted (protects against a concurrent edit). One update op through the kernel writer. `markdown` may parse to SEVERAL sibling blocks (e.g. a paragraph followed by a list): the target keeps its id and takes the first, the rest are inserted right after it with fresh ids — the response carries `id` (the target) and `ids` (all resulting blocks, in order). A list item may likewise be replaced by a multi-item list (`- a\n- b`), yielding sibling items. Task state is settable flat as `checked` (the same name reads flatten to — `from blocks where checked`), folded into attrs and synced to the `[ ]`/`[x]` in the raw. The general `attrs` bag is still accepted; note every OTHER block attr (heading `level`, code `lang`, list `ordered`) is derived from the markdown, so set those by editing `markdown`, not attrs.
blocks_move: Move block(s) under a new parent at a position. `blocks` are block refs; `to` (the parent) is a block ref (a container — a leaf parent is `type_mismatch`, as for blocks_insert), or the blocks' OWN document (id or path) to move them to its top level — moving to ANOTHER document's root is not expressible (target_missing): anchor on a block in that document with `at` {before|after} instead. `at` is "end"/"start"/{before|after: <ref>}. Optional `expect.parent_children_hash` is the destination-parent CAS (as blocks_insert: the destination parent's CURRENT direct child ids joined by ",", sha256 hex), checked once for the whole run before anything moves — `stale_expectation` with `data.current.parent_children_hash` if the destination's children changed; `content_hash` is meaningless here and not accepted. One move op through the kernel writer.
blocks_remove: Remove block(s) (the resurrection pool catches regret). `blocks` are refs; removing a block removes its whole subtree, and a set that names both a container and some of its descendants (e.g. every id of a section straight from docs_read include_ids) is fine — it collapses to the top-most blocks and `removed` lists everything that left. One remove op through the kernel writer. To delete a whole document use docs_delete.
blocks_split: Split a block at UTF-8 byte offset(s) into consecutive blocks. `id` is the block's id (or a ref); `at` is a list of integer byte offsets into the block's raw bytes (spec/mutate §2.5; an offset inside a multi-byte character rounds down to its start). CAS is pinned to the block's current bytes server-side. One split op through the kernel writer.
blocks_merge: Merge adjacent blocks into the first, joined by `separator` (default a blank line). `blocks` are refs (≥2). One merge op through the kernel writer.
blocks_check: Macro: check (or uncheck with checked:false) the given task blocks. `ids` are the blocks' ids (or refs). Expands to update(attrs:{checked}) per block, CAS-pinned, applied via the same changeset machinery (tasks_complete { blocks } before surface 3.0).
nodes_set: Macro: surgically set one editable property of a projected node (e.g. a link's `name` text or `value` target, a task's `checked`). `id` is the node's id (from `query` over `from nodes` — the one tool that addresses `nodes` rows), `prop` the property, `value` its new value. Resolves the node to its block and rewrites only that node's span, applying one update op. Nodes are read-only projections — this is the affordance to edit what a node represents without hand-rewriting the block. Errors node_not_editable (with the editable prop list) when the kind/prop has no editor. (node_set before surface 3.0.)
blocks_append: Macro: append markdown INTO a block, by what the block is. `id` is a block's id (or a ref). A HEADING: the `text` is inserted at the end of its section range (before the next heading of equal or higher level) — the former sections_append. A CONTAINER (a list, list item, task, blockquote or table — anything the kernel accepts as a parent): inserted at the end of its children (`blocks_insert { to: <id>, at: "end" }`). A LEAF (a paragraph, code fence, …) is `block_not_container` — append means "into", never a sibling insert; place after it with `blocks_insert { to: <its parent>, at: { after: <id> } }`. Expands to one insert op; to append at a whole document's end, or inside a section named by its heading TEXT, use docs_append.
docs_append: Macro: append markdown to a document — at its END, or at the end of one of its sections when `section` names a heading by its TEXT (`"Setup"`; an ATX spelling `"## Setup"` is accepted). The journal/log/running-note primitive. ADDITIVE and identity-preserving, NOT a whole-body replace: the `text` is parsed into blocks and inserted as NEW blocks after the existing ones (at the document's top level, or inside the section's range), so every existing block keeps its stable `b_` id (omgbase deliberately has no whole-body `docs_put` — see mcp-api). Expands to a single insert op; commits atomically through the same kernel path as `apply`, returning the new revision(s) and the inserted block ids. Address the document by `id` or `path` (at least one). The document must already exist — a missing doc errors `doc_missing` (creating one is docs_create's job, never this); a `section` matching no heading in it is `parent_missing`, one matching several is `ambiguous_heading` with `candidates[{ id, doc_id }]` — pass that heading's id to blocks_append, which appends into a block by its id.
links_retarget: Macro: rewrite ONE link destination everywhere it is linked — the single-pair form of links_repair (same matching rules: whole link destinations only, leading `/` optional, fragments preserved; prose/inline code/code fences untouched). Scope source docs with `path_glob`. ALWAYS call with dry_run:true first to preview `hits` + `pairs` (the dry run plans through the kernel, so it fails exactly where the apply would), then dry_run:false to apply.
links_stale: READ-ONLY link health: surfaces DANGLING internal links — links whose target path has NO live document (stored as a `phantom:` edge; a doc created at that path auto-resolves them). Returns `stale[]` (each a link row under the `links` target's names: `doc_id`, `path` (the source document), `block_id` (null for a frontmatter edge), predicate, provenance, dst_kind, `target` = the canonical missing path, `/`-rooted like every path the surface returns (e.g. `/guides/old.md`), `authored` = the destination text exactly as written in the source block (e.g. `/guides/old.md#Setup`; null for frontmatter edges), `anchor`, and reason `dangling_doc`), plus `externalCount` (http(s) links — UNVERIFIABLE here, never marked broken, since reachability needs network I/O the engine won't do), `totalOpenEdges`, and `truncated` (capped by `limit`, default 500). `summary:true` returns counts only — `staleCount`, `byTarget[{target,count}]`, `bySource[{path,count}]`, `externalCount`, `totalOpenEdges` — for a repo-wide audit in one small call. Scope the SOURCE docs with `path_glob` (e.g. "journal/*"; `*` matches across `/`). Fix the reported targets with `links_repair` (batch) or `links_retarget` (single): either `target` or `authored` works as `from`. Anchors (#heading/^ref) into an existing doc are NOT verified in v1. Contrast docs_read/query which answer 'what does this doc say', not 'which of its links are broken'.
links_repair: Macro: BULK stale-link repair — rewrite one or MANY LINK DESTINATIONS in ONE changeset. Pass `repairs` (an array of {from,to}) to fix several dangling targets — e.g. those surfaced by links_stale — at once; a single {from_target,to_target} pair is also accepted. MATCHING: `from` must be the WHOLE destination of a Markdown link/image `[t](dest)`, a wikilink `[[dest]]`/`[[dest|alias]]`, or a bare-path inline field `key:: /dest` — a leading `/` is optional on either side (so links_stale's `target` or `authored` both work), and a trailing `#heading`/`^ref` fragment on the link is kept and re-appended to `to`. NOT rewritten: prose mentions, inline code, `code_fence` blocks, longer paths that merely contain `from`, and frontmatter values (use docs_set_meta). Scope source docs with `path_glob` (as in links_stale). Ops coalesce to one update per TOP-MOST block (a list and its items count once), so a batch never trips over its own re-minted children. Returns `hits[{id,path,oldRaw,newRaw}]` (the rewritten block and its document) and `pairs[{from,to,hits}]` (per-pair destination counts; 0 = nothing matched). ALWAYS call with dry_run:true first — the dry run plans through the kernel (returns `diffs`), so it fails exactly where the apply would — then dry_run:false to apply.
docs_create: Create a new document at `path` (the new document's path, either form) from complete file bytes (`markdown`), with optional structured `frontmatter`; returns `{ id, path, committed }`. Fails path_taken if it already exists. dry_run:true validates and returns the would-be file under `diffs` (committed:false) without writing.
docs_move: Rename a document to a new path (`to_path`, `/`-rooted or bare; the result `{ id, path, committed, retargeted, dangling }` reports the rooted form); the document is addressed by `id` or `path`. Block identity and history are preserved, and the inbound links FOLLOW it: every link written against the old path (Markdown links/images, wikilinks, bare-path inline fields — anchors, link text, titles and code spans preserved, absolute vs relative style kept) is rewritten to the new path in the same call as one CAS-checked changeset, so a move never leaves the graph broken. Fails path_taken if the destination exists. The result carries `retargeted` (the touched blocks/docs) and `dangling` — what could NOT be rewritten, i.e. frontmatter relations (block null; fix with docs_set_meta). Pass `retarget_inbound:false` to opt out for the rarer intent that the old path become unbound: the links are left as written, listed in `dangling` ({doc_id, path, block_id, target, anchor, field?} per occurrence — a link row under the `links` target's names) and reported by links_stale (their edges become `phantom:<old path>`); links already written against the new path start resolving to this doc either way. dry_run:true validates and returns the plan — `dangling`, `retargeted`, and the per-file `diffs` (the old path emptied, the new path filled, plus the rewritten sources) — without renaming or committing.
docs_delete: Delete a document: tombstone it and its live blocks (resurrection-poolable) and remove the file. Address it by `id` or `path`. dry_run:true validates and returns the file's removal under `diffs` without deleting.
docs_set_meta: Surgical frontmatter patch: set the given keys and/or unset named keys on the document addressed by `id` or `path`, re-ingesting it. Other frontmatter is preserved. dry_run:true validates and returns the rewritten file under `diffs` without writing.
docs_update: Whole-document update with smart identity preservation. Submit the complete proposed `content` for a document (`id` or `path`); the engine reconciles it against the current tree, preserving stable block ids for structure that is recognizably the same (edits, moves, reorders), minting for new structure, and tombstoning removals — then commits the derived opset through the kernel write path. Frontmatter changes are applied too. dry_run:true is the PLAN-ONLY call (docs_plan_update before surface 3.0): nothing is written and the result is `{ opset, plan, result: null }` — the exact kernel ops (insert/update/move/remove) it would run, each annotated with its identity consequence (disposition, confidence, reason), a summary (preserved/updated/moved/created/removed) and a human-readable plan; the opset carries `precondition: { id, path, baseRevision, hash }` (the document's revision and hash at plan time) and `converges`, verified by replaying the ops (a divergence names the first differing byte and the proposed block in `diagnostics[]`). Use the dry run to inspect identity effects before committing, then call again without it. Conflicts (the doc changed since planning) fail stale_plan — re-run. A plan whose replay cannot reproduce `content` byte-for-byte fails plan_not_convergent; the message names the first divergent byte and the proposed block (index/type) that failed to round-trip (full diagnostics in `data.diagnostics`). This is the dry run's opset + apply(opset).
observe: SYNC INGEST (ADR-014): record `content` as the current authoritative bytes for `path`, committed as an OBSERVED-origin revision — a write *around* the engine, the way a human/external edit is recorded. Contrast docs_update, which is api-origin (a write *through* the engine, agent intent); both reconcile the new bytes against the current block tree and preserve stable ids, but the origin differs (and thus the change-feed semantics and matcher path). This is the file→DB direction for an out-of-process synchronizer: it never writes a file, so it works on a headless/sourceless server with no working tree. Idempotent: bytes whose hash already equals the stored revision are an ECHO — no commit (`echo:true`, `rev:null`). Bytes with git conflict markers are still ingested (opaque) and the doc is flagged (`conflicted:true`). To mirror a deletion, use `observe_delete` (an observed, resurrection-pooled tombstone — not `docs_delete`, which is an intentional api-origin removal that also unlinks the file). Returns `{ id, path, rev, commitId, converged, echo, conflicted, dispositions }` — the document's row attributes plus a disposition summary (how identity threaded). `path` is a FILE event's path from the store's layer, not a row locator, so it keeps its name.
observe_many: BATCH sync ingest (ADR-014): observe several files at once — the batch form of `observe`. Give `files` as an array of `{path, content}`; each is echo-gated and reconciled independently, all under one timestamp and a single resurrection-pool sweep (cheaper than N `observe` calls for an initial walk or a large checkpoint). Returns one result per input file (same shape as `observe`). Mirror deletions with `observe_delete`, one path at a time.
observe_delete: SYNC DELETE (ADR-014): record that `path` left the source scope — tombstone the live doc as an OBSERVED deletion (its blocks are pooled for resurrection if the path reappears; no file is removed, since it is already gone from the source). The deletion counterpart to `observe`, for a synchronizer mirroring an external delete. Idempotent: a path with no live doc is a no-op (`deleted:false`). Contrast `docs_delete` — an api-origin, intentional, non-pooled removal that also unlinks the working-tree file.
blocks_history: A block's biography: the commits that touched the block `id` names, with disposition kind/confidence/reason, newest first (history_node before surface 3.0 — it always took a block id and returned the block's changes). Not repo-scoped: block ids are global.
docs_diff: Block-grain diff between two revisions of a document: `[{ kind: added|removed|changed, id (the block), before?, after? }]` in that order. Address the document by `id` or `path` (at least one); `from_rev`/`to_rev` are revision ids (from docs_history, changes_since or blocks_history). Contrast docs_diff_unified, the unified text diff. (diff before surface 3.0.)
docs_diff_unified: Unified diff between two revisions of a document (the `omg diff` rendering): returns `{ id, path, from, to, diff }` where `diff` is a unified diff of the two revisions' file texts — for each revision exactly the bytes docs_read_at returns, so hunk line numbers are real file lines (Myers shortest edit script; `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` hunks with 3 lines of context; lines prefixed `-`, `+` or a space; no file header; identical texts → ""). Address the document by `id` or `path` (at least one). `from_rev`/`to_rev` default to the previous and current revisions ('what did the last commit change here'). Contrast `docs_diff`, which returns block-grain added/removed/changed entries. (diff_unified before surface 3.0.)
docs_read_at: TIME-TRAVEL read: the whole file bytes of a document AS OF a past revision — `raw` is the reconstructed source at that `rev` (fences/tables/list markers preserved), plus `id`/`path` (the path as of that revision)/`rev`. Use this to audit or answer 'what did this doc say at revision N', or to fetch the exact prior text before reverting. Get a `rev` from docs_diff, blocks_history, docs_history or changes_since. Contrast: docs_read = current bytes; docs_diff = block-grain changes BETWEEN two revisions. `renderedHashMatch` is true when the reconstruction is byte-for-byte the file at that revision; it can be false for an old revision ONLY when the document's leading/frontmatter trivia (separator bytes, not block content) changed since — block content always reconstructs faithfully. `properties` are CURRENT values (propertiesAreCurrent:true), since property history is not stored. Address the document by `id` or `path` plus a `rev` id.
docs_history: VERSION HISTORY of matching documents, grouped BY DOCUMENT: for each doc (`id`, `path`, `deleted`, `currentRev`), its ordered revision list (oldest→newest) with `rev`/`seq`/`commit`/`updated_at`/`origin`/`actor`/`hash`/`isCurrent`. Give `path_glob` (e.g. "journal/*" — `*` matches ACROSS `/`, so journal/* and journal/** are equivalent) OR a single document by `id` or `path`; at least one is required. `hash` (hex of the revision's rendered file hash) lets you spot no-op vs real changes. Feed a returned `rev` into `docs_read_at` (whole doc AT that rev) or `docs_diff` (block-grain changes BETWEEN two revs). By default only live docs; `include_deleted:true` also returns tombstoned docs (their history is intact for audit). `limit` caps DOCUMENTS returned (default 50) with a `truncated` flag. Contrast `changes_since`: a repo-wide COMMIT feed, not this per-document view.
changes_since: The change feed: commit digests after a cursor (repo commit seq) with one-line summaries. Each digest's `revisions[]` carries `{ id, path, hash }` (hash = hex of the revision's rendered file hash; the same shape an apply result's revisions have), so a synchronizer can decide 'changed vs echo' without a follow-up docs_read. Filter by `origin` (api/observed/import) to ignore commits a given writer produced. Poll with your last cursor to cheaply re-orient after time away. Paging: `cursor` is the last digest's `seq` (a dense per-REPO order — a cursor is only meaningful against the same `repo` it came from); pass it back while `truncated` is true. `head` is the repo's current max seq: an empty page with cursor == head means nothing new, cursor > head means the cursor belongs to a different repo/server.
repos_status: Repo counts (`{ id, slug, rootPath, docs, blocks, commits, openEdges, unconverged, disk }`): docs, blocks, commits, open edges, unconverged doc count, and on-disk drift. `disk` reports a READ-ONLY scan of the working tree vs the DB: `changed` (files edited on disk but not re-ingested), `deleted` (docs whose file is gone from disk), `untracked` (new *.md not yet ingested), and `checked` (false when the server has no working-tree path — disk agreement is then UNVERIFIED, not clean).
sync_status: Watcher/sync state: last commit seq, last checkpoint, and whether the repo is convergent. `convergent` is true ONLY when the DB is internally converged AND a working-tree scan ran (`diskChecked`) AND found no drift (`disk.changed`/`deleted`/`untracked` all 0). If the server has no working-tree path, `diskChecked` is false and `convergent` is false — a green light is never shown while disk freshness is unverified, so an agent can trust `convergent: true` to mean not stale.
repos: List the repos in this workspace: `{ repos: [{ slug, hasSource }] }`. A client addresses any of them by passing that `slug` as the `repo` argument to another tool (omit `repo` ⇒ the server's default repo). Use repos_status for per-repo counts/convergence.
version: Which engine and which versions you are talking to: `{ engine: "typescript"|"rust", version, components: { <package>: <version> }, specs: { oqx, format, reconcile, store, properties, graph, search, mutate, sync, surface, cli }, schema, mcp: { protocol, sdk? }, runtime, commit, built }`. `version` is the serving binary's own; `components` every omgbase package it is built from; `specs` the spec versions it implements (compile-time constants); `schema` the database's `PRAGMA user_version`; `commit`/`built` the build's git revision and RFC 3339 time (null when unknown). No arguments, no repo scope.
